schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Recurrent or metastatic incurable nasopharyngeal carcinoma after platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: EBV positive vs negative (local pathology); ECOG 0-1 vs 2. Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 28-day cycles. Safety lead-in in the first 6 patients per arm (12 total), with accrual paused until all complete 8 weeks.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily + nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Nivolumab and ipilimumab for a maximum of 2 years; cabozantinib may continue beyond 2 years per investigator.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 2 years after treatment discontinuation or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival, cabozantinib-nivolumab-ipilimumab vs nivolumab-ipilimumab.

eligibility: Histologically documented nasopharyngeal carcinoma, any WHO type (keratinizing, non-keratinizing, basaloid squamous), regardless of EBV, HPV, p16, or PD-L1 status.
Recurrent, metastatic, incurable disease previously treated with platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade (first or second line), with immunotherapy part of the most recent line.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 with at least one measurable lesion not previously irradiated.
No more than 2 prior lines of systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic NPC; no prior VEGFR-targeted therapy.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS 0-2.

ANC ≥ 1,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, creatinine ≤ 1.5 mg/dL or CrCl ≥ 30 (MDRD), total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert < 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).

No chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 3 weeks (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C) before registration; palliative limited-field RT allowed if repeat imaging shows no new bone metastases and the irradiated lesion is not a target lesion.

Recovered from prior therapy toxicity to grade ≤ 1 (except alopecia); no prior life-threatening immune-related events likely to recur (severe pneumonitis, grade 4 bullous dermatitis/DRESS, autoimmune encephalitis, transverse myelitis, myocarditis).
No active tumor bleeding or radiographic major blood vessel infiltration.

Treated brain metastases allowed if imaging 3 weeks after CNS-directed therapy shows no progression; active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease allowed if immediate CNS treatment is not required and unlikely during cycle 1.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that might recur and affect vital organs or need immunosuppression (e.g., MS, myasthenia gravis, GBS, SLE, scleroderma, IBD, SJS/TEN); vitiligo and replaced endocrinopathies allowed.

No systemic corticosteroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days of registration (topical, inhaled, intra-articular, adrenal replacement, and brief courses allowed).

No warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors such as clopidogrel; low-dose aspirin, LMWH, and stable rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban (without brain metastases) allowed.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment. Prior solid organ transplant allowed.
No prior malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Able to swallow oral medication.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration).

schema.label: Step 1: Registration/Randomization
schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma, age ≥ 12. Treatment begins ≤ 28 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior systemic therapy (treatment naive vs ≥ 1 prior line); corticosteroid-producing tumor (yes vs no). Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO once daily, continuous, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cemiplimab 350 mg IV day 1 every 21 days + cabozantinib 40 mg PO once daily. Cemiplimab maximum 2 years; cabozantinib alone may continue afterward until progression or toxicity.

schema.label: Step 2: Crossover (Arm C)
schema.text: Arm A patients with RECIST progression may re-register within 4 weeks (± 1 week) to cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 21 days + cabozantinib daily (no re-escalation of a previously reduced cabozantinib dose); cemiplimab maximum 2 years.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 4 years from registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1, cabozantinib-cemiplimab vs cabozantinib alone.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically confirmed adrenocortical carcinoma, locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic, with disease evaluable by RECIST 1.1.
Up to 3 prior systemic lines in the unresectable/recurrent/metastatic setting (EDP-M counts as 1 line); treatment-naive patients allowed.
No prior cabozantinib or other cMET inhibitor, anti-CTLA-4, or anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy.

Prior RT, cytotoxic chemotherapy, or targeted therapy allowed if completed ≥ 14 days before registration with toxicity recovered to grade ≤ 1; lesions irradiated within 1 month cannot be index lesions.
Mitotane within 6 months: must be stopped ≥ 28 days before registration with a mitotane level < 2 mg/L.
Age ≥ 12 years and BSA ≥ 1.2 m2. ECOG 0-2 (age ≥ 18), Lansky ≥ 50 (age 12-15), or Karnofsky ≥ 50 (age 16-17).

ANC ≥ 1,000/mcL without growth factor within 2 weeks, platelets ≥ 100,000/mcL, hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert ≤ 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, UPCR ≤ 1 mg/mg, CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min.
Adrenal steroid production assessed (random ACTH and cortisol) within 3 months before registration, for stratification.

Cardiac: NYHA class II or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; no congenital long QT, no myocarditis, no MI or unstable angina within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypertension (sustained ≥ 150/90 mmHg) within 14 days.

No GI conditions with bleeding or perforation risk within 6 months (active ulcer, bleeding endoluminal metastasis, IBD), no GI perforation within 6 months, no tumor invading the GI tract within 28 days, and no pancreatitis.
No endobronchial lesions of main or lobar bronchi, no tumor infiltrating major pulmonary vessels or encasing any major blood vessel, and no hemoptysis > 2.5 mL within 3 months.
No history of pneumonitis.

No brain metastases or cranial epidural disease unless treated with RT and/or surgery (including radiosurgery), stable ≥ 4 weeks, neurologically asymptomatic, and off corticosteroids at treatment start.
No major surgery within 2 weeks or minor surgery within 10 days; no fracture or non-healing wound within 28 days.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that may recur and affect vital organs or require immunosuppression; vitiligo and replaced endocrinopathies allowed. No steroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent.

No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (stop 14 days before), and no warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors within 5 days; low-dose aspirin, LMWH, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban allowed.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with assessment.
Able to swallow tablets. Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before registration).

Step 2 (crossover to Arm C): RECIST progression on Arm A cabozantinib, re-registration within 4 weeks (± 1 week) of progression, all Step 1 criteria met, not discontinued from (or meeting discontinuation criteria for) cabozantinib due to toxicity, pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before re-registration.

schema.text: Platinum-refractory recurrent or metastatic HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, hypopharynx), PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1, no prior therapy in the recurrent/metastatic setting. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Time to progression after concurrent CRT (definitive or postoperative): 0 to ≤ 3 months vs > 3 to 6 months; local PD-L1 CPS < 20 vs ≥ 20. Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.text: 42-day (6-week) cycles

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Pembrolizumab 400 mg IV day 1 every 42 days (200 mg every 21 days not allowed).

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Lead-in cetuximab 500 mg/m2 IV on day -14 before cycle 1, then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV day 1 every 42 days + cetuximab 500 mg/m2 IV days 1, 15, and 29 (every 2 weeks). Grade ≥ 3 infusion reaction to the lead-in ends cetuximab.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: Up to 18 cycles, or until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 5 years from registration or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival, pembrolizumab + cetuximab vs pembrolizumab.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed HNSCC of the oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx; nasopharynx and other sites excluded; unknown primary only with study chair approval.
Recurrent and/or metastatic disease incurable by local therapy, previously untreated in the recurrent/metastatic setting, with measurable disease.
Platinum-refractory: progression during or ≤ 29 weeks after completing definitive chemoradiation or adjuvant (postoperative) therapy.
PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1.
Oropharynx primaries must be HPV-negative by p16 IHC and/or HPV ISH (CLIA-certified ctHPV DNA acceptable if no tissue).
Any radiation therapy completed > 10 days before registration.
Prior neoadjuvant or induction anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or cetuximab in the curative setting allowed only if the last dose was ≥ 26 weeks before registration without progression during that treatment.
No live vaccine within 30 days; no systemic steroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression within 7 days; no grade ≥ 3 hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or cetuximab.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS ≤ 2.

ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed), creatinine ≤ 1.5 x ULN or CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN or direct bilirubin < ULN, AST/ALT ≤ 3.0 x ULN (< 5.0 x ULN with liver metastases).

Treated brain metastases allowed if imaging after CNS-directed therapy shows no progression; active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease allowed if immediate CNS treatment is not required and unlikely during cycle 1.

No history of active myocarditis, any pneumonitis, or diffuse idiopathic or immune-mediated interstitial lung disease; no prior solid organ transplant. NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.
HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration).

FDRs are contacted with a recruitment script, consented with incomplete disclosure, and registered. Stratified by Lynch syndrome (yes vs no), number of eligible FDRs (2-4 vs 5-7 vs ≥ 8), and variant penetrance (high vs moderate/low); Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Study entry
schema.text: Age 1 month to < 6 years, KMT2A-rearranged leukemia (diagnosed at < 2 years) that is refractory or in first marrow relapse, CNS1/CNS2, WBC < 50,000/µL. Single-arm phase 2 with a safety lead-in (RP2D) then an expansion phase.

schema.label: Regimen A (ALL, ALAL, or MPAL phenotype; investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycle 1: revumenib + 3-drug re-induction (prednisone/prednisolone BID days 1-28, vincristine days 1, 8, 15, 22, calaspargase pegol day 4, IT methotrexate days 1 and 8). Day 29 marrow, then callback for cycle 2 dose level. Cycle 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT day 0). Early progressive disease during cycle 1 may move straight to cycle 2, then a third FLA cycle.

schema.label: Regimen B (AML phenotype, or ALL/ALAL/MPAL by investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycles 1 and 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT).

schema.label: Revumenib dosing in combination
schema.text: Age ≥ 6 months: DL1 130 mg/m2 Q12H (DL2 160, DL0 95). Age 2 to < 6 months: 100 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 80). Age 1 to < 2 months: 70 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 56). Oral liquid; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors not allowed in combination cycles.

schema.label: Disease evaluation
schema.text: Marrow day 29 (re-induction) or days 29-35 by count recovery (FLA cycles; by day 36 regardless), with central MRD. Patients not meeting treatment failure criteria continue. May leave at any time for HSCT or cellular therapy.

schema.label: Revumenib monotherapy
schema.text: Up to 12 cycles while M1 marrow is maintained without Rel-M1: 160 mg/m2 Q12H for age ≥ 6 months (95 mg/m2 with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor azole); 100 mg/m2 Q12H for age 2 to < 6 months (60 mg/m2 with azole).

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: RP2D of revumenib with chemotherapy in R/R KMT2A-R ALL, and MRD-negative remission rate in patients older than 6 months at enrollment with R/R infant KMT2A-R ALL.

eligibility: Age 1 month to < 6 years at enrollment, with initial leukemia diagnosis at < 2 years.
KMT2A-rearranged ALL, ALAL, or MPAL (lineage switch to AML allowed if prior KMT2A-R ALL/ALAL/MPAL documented), with KMT2A-R confirmed by central cytogenetics/FISH review (submitted by day 10).

Primary refractory (no remission after at least 2 frontline courses; 2 courses plus 1 blinatumomab course allowed, nothing beyond) or untreated first marrow relapse (M3; M2 with 1 confirmatory test; or M1 with 2 confirmatory tests at ≥ 1%).
CNS1 or CNS2 with no neurologic signs of CNS leukemia; CNS3 may receive prior IT therapy to reach CNS1/2. Prior CNS chloroma requires no radiographic CNS disease. No isolated extramedullary leukemia.
WBC < 50,000/µL at enrollment; hydroxyurea and/or corticosteroids allowed for up to 7 days before enrollment.
Lansky ≥ 50% if age ≥ 12 months. Able to take enteral medication (PO, NG, NJ, ND, or G-tube).

Washouts: ≥ 14 days after cytotoxic therapy (≥ 7 days if relapse on maintenance); ≥ 7 days for non-myelosuppressive agents; ≥ 21 days for antibodies (blinatumomab ≥ 3 days); ≥ 84 days after allogeneic HSCT; ≥ 28 days after DLI or cellular therapy; ≥ 14 days after local XRT, ≥ 84 days after TBI, craniospinal RT, or ≥ 50% pelvis, ≥ 42 days after other substantial marrow RT. Prior FLA allowed.
Creatinine at or below age maximum (0.4 mg/dL at 1 to < 6 months, 0.5 at 6-12 months, 0.6 at 1 to < 2 years, 0.8 at 2 to < 6 years) or measured GFR/CrCl ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Direct bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN and ALT ≤ 135 U/L, unless disease related.
Shortening fraction ≥ 27% or EF ≥ 50%, and QTcF < 450 ms (triplicate average).
No Down syndrome, bone marrow failure syndrome (Bloom, ataxia-telangiectasia, Fanconi, Kostmann, Shwachman), or secondary KMT2A-R leukemia after cytotoxic chemotherapy for a prior cancer.
No congenital long QT, CHF, or uncontrolled arrhythmia within 6 months.

No active uncontrolled infection (positive blood culture or infectious fever within 48 hours, positive fungal culture or active invasive fungal treatment within 30 days, viral or protozoal infection needing IV therapy). HIV allowed if on non-interacting antiretrovirals with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No active acute GVHD > grade 0 or chronic GVHD > mild (skin-only exceptions); off systemic anti-GVHD agents > 7 days. No prior solid organ transplant.
No prior revumenib (other menin inhibitors allowed). No Charcot-Marie-Tooth if receiving Regimen A.
No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or moderate/strong inducers (stopped ≥ 5 half-lives before therapy), no other investigational or anticancer agents.

Reopens enrollment for patients younger than 6 months with a new age-based revumenib dosing strategy, clarifies timing of eligibility labs, prohibits strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers throughout therapy, and updates dose modifications and drug monographs.

schema.label: Step 1: Enrollment and steroid prephase
schema.text: APEC14B1 enrollment with diagnostic sample, then AALL2321 consent. Prednisone or prednisolone 20 mg/m2/dose TID days 1-7 for all patients (may extend 2 days awaiting KMT2A FISH). KMT2A status from COG-approved cytogenetics lab, entered by day 10 and centrally confirmed.

schema.label: Step 2: Callback and assignment by KMT2A status
schema.text: KMT2A-R: slot reservation, then randomization 1:1 (stratified by age at diagnosis) to Arm A or Arm B. KMT2A-germline: assigned to Arm C. The KMT2A-R safety phase cohort (venetoclax in place of cytarabine in induction, rolling six) closed with Amendment #3A; venetoclax DL2 (14 days) carried forward.

arms.label: Arm A (KMT2A-R control)
arms.text: 5-drug infant induction (35 days: daunorubicin days 1-2, cytarabine days 1-14, vincristine, dexamethasone, calaspargase pegol day 4, triple IT), blinatumomab block 1, split consolidation (cyclophosphamide/cytarabine/mercaptopurine, 2 x 14 days), MARMA, blinatumomab block 2, delayed intensification, maintenance (daily mercaptopurine, weekly oral methotrexate) to 2 years from start of MARMA.

arms.label: Arm B (KMT2A-R venetoclax)
arms.text: 4-drug induction with venetoclax days 1-14 (age-based mg/kg, replacing cytarabine), then the Arm A backbone with venetoclax added by cohort: Cohort 1 MARMA part 2 (with high-dose cytarabine); Cohort 2 consolidation; Cohort 3 consolidation and MARMA (if Cohorts 1 and 2 are safe); Cohort 4 induction only (if Cohorts 1-3 suspended).

schema.label: Arm C (KMT2A-germline, non-randomized)
schema.text: 5-drug infant induction, blinatumomab block 1, consolidation, interim maintenance I, blinatumomab block 2, delayed intensification, interim maintenance II, maintenance (COG SR-High backbone, as in AALL1731) to 2 years from start of IM I.

schema.label: Blinatumomab blocks
schema.text: 28-day continuous infusion, 15 mcg/m2/day (max 28 mcg/day); for M2/M3 marrow at end of induction, 5 mcg/m2/day days 1-7 then 15 mcg/m2/day days 8-28.

schema.label: Response gates
schema.text: CNS1 by end of induction. MRD < 1% at end of blinatumomab block 1, MRD < 0.01% by end of consolidation, and no residual non-CNS extramedullary disease at EOB1; otherwise treatment failure and off protocol therapy.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Safety and tolerability of venetoclax with chemotherapy and two blinatumomab blocks in infants with KMT2A-R ALL, and end-of-induction MRD-negative remission rate with vs without venetoclax (randomized).

No prior cytotoxic chemotherapy, except prednisone, prednisolone, or methylprednisolone for ≤ 72 hours within 7 days before enrollment, hydroxyurea for ≤ 72 hours within 7 days, and one IT cytarabine or methotrexate within 7 days.
No dexamethasone within 28 days before protocol therapy, except a single dose around sedation for airway edema.

reviewed.notes: Eligibility is short in the protocol itself (7 items); organ function is not an entry criterion. Existing schema and eligibility were table-of-contents text.

schema.label: Low Risk (all ages): active surveillance
schema.text: Stage I extracranial GCT after surgery, no chemotherapy. Strata: ovarian immature teratoma (any stage or grade, AFP ≤ 1,000 ng/mL, normal β-HCG); stage I testicular seminoma; stage I non-seminoma MGCT at any site (yolk sac, embryonal, or choriocarcinoma). Post-op markers must be falling. Tumor markers and imaging surveillance; patients with rising markers or recurrence may transfer to a Standard Risk arm by late randomization (not seminoma).

schema.label: Standard Risk 1 (age < 11): Randomize
schema.text: COG stage II-IV extracranial MGCT, any site (IGCCC does not apply). 21-day cycles.

arms.label: CEb x 4
arms.text: Carboplatin 600 mg/m2 day 1 (max 1200 mg), etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 day 1 (max 30 units); BSA-banded doses below 0.6 m2.

arms.label: PEb x 4
arms.text: Cisplatin 20 mg/m2 days 1-5, etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 day 1.

schema.label: Standard Risk 2 (age 11 to < 25): Randomize
schema.text: Ovarian COG stage II-III (FIGO IC-III) or testicular COG stage II-IV and IGCCC good risk. 21-day cycles.

arms.label: BEC x 3
arms.text: Carboplatin 600 mg/m2 day 1 (max 1200 mg), etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 days 1, 8, 15.

arms.label: BEP x 3
arms.text: Cisplatin 20 mg/m2 days 1-5, etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-5, bleomycin 15 units/m2 days 1, 8, 15.

schema.label: Post-chemotherapy evaluation
schema.text: Markers and imaging within 6 weeks of day 21 of the last cycle; second-look resection of residual masses ≥ 1 cm within 6 weeks of imaging. Routine consolidation cycles are not recommended; further therapy for viable tumor is at physician discretion. Myeloid growth factor after each cycle.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Low Risk: 2-year OS of at least 95.7% for stage I MGCT and at least 88% for ovarian immature teratoma with surgery plus surveillance. Standard Risk: EFS with carboplatin- vs cisplatin-based therapy (CEb vs PEb in SR1, BEC vs BEP in SR2).

eligibility: Low Risk: no age limit. SR1: age < 11 years. SR2: age ≥ 11 and < 25 years.

Newly diagnosed extracranial GCT: stage I for Low Risk strata, malignant GCT stage II or higher for Standard Risk, with histology and stage as defined per stratum (yolk sac component must be more than microscopic when it is the only malignant element).

Histologic confirmation required, except recurrence of resected non-seminoma with markers > 5 x ULN on 2 measurements at least 1 week apart, or markers AFP ≥ 500 ng/mL or HCG ≥ 500 IU/L with typical imaging when biopsy or upfront resection is not appropriate.
SR2 testicular: IGCCC good risk using post-op markers (AFP < 1,000 ng/mL, β-HCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, LDH < 3.0 x normal).
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16).

Standard Risk only: CrCl or GFR ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum; total bilirubin ≤ 2 x ULN and AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (unless Gilbert's, liver involvement, or vanishing bile duct syndrome); ANC ≥ 750/mm3 and platelets ≥ 75,000/mm3.
No pure ovarian or extragonadal dysgerminoma/seminoma, pure mature teratoma, primary CNS GCT, or GCT with somatic malignant transformation.
No poor-risk GCT (age ≥ 11 with COG stage IV ovarian, stage II-IV extragonadal, or IGCCC intermediate/poor risk testicular).
No prior radiation therapy, except CNS irradiation of brain metastases in SR1 patients.
Standard Risk: no significant pre-existing respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin.
Standard Risk: not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

eligibility: COG/NCTN sites use the Appendix 7 criteria, which differ from the main ANZUP protocol.
Age ≥ 11 and ≤ 50 years at randomization.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed GCT (non-seminoma or seminoma), or AFP ≥ 1000 ng/mL and/or HCG ≥ 5000 IU/L without histology when metastatic pattern, high burden, and urgency fit GCT.
Primary in testis, ovary, retroperitoneum, or mediastinum; metastatic disease or non-testicular primary.

Intermediate or poor risk by modified IGCCC: non-seminoma intermediate (testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP 1000-10,000 ng/mL, HCG 5000-50,000 IU/L, or LDH 3-10 x ULN); non-seminoma poor (mediastinal primary, non-pulmonary visceral mets, AFP > 10,000, HCG > 50,000, or LDH > 10 x ULN); seminoma with non-pulmonary visceral mets and normal AFP; or ovarian MGCT FIGO/COG stage IV. Post-orchiectomy markers used.
ANC ≥ 1.0 x 10^9/L and platelets ≥ 100 x 10^9/L.
Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 2.0 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST/ALT ≤ 2.5 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).
Age ≥ 18: CrCl ≥ 60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, or measured GFR if borderline). Age < 18: CrCl or GFR > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum.
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16). Treatment able to start within 14 days of OPEN enrollment.
No prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, except pure seminoma relapsing after adjuvant radiotherapy or 1-2 doses of single-agent carboplatin.
No other primary malignancy except treated non-melanoma skin cancer, GCT, or a cancer treated at least 5 years ago without recurrence.
No cardiac disease preventing cisplatin hydration, no respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin, no grade ≥ 2 neuropathy, and no clinically significant hearing loss or tinnitus.
No severe concurrent illness or infection. No known allergy to study drugs.
Not pregnant; negative pregnancy test within 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Age 11-50 years, intermediate- or poor-risk metastatic GCT (testis, ovary, retroperitoneum, or mediastinum) needing first-line chemotherapy. COG/NCTN arm of ANZUP 1302 (P3BEP); randomization in Flexetrials/REDCap within 10 days of starting chemotherapy.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: ECOG PS 0-1 vs 2-3; IGCCC intermediate vs poor; mediastinal vs other primary; brain metastases present vs absent; induction chemotherapy present vs absent; age, sex, site.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: N = 500. Total planned chemotherapy 12 weeks in both arms. Bleomycin 30 units per dose if age ≥ 16, 15 units/m2 (max 30 units) if < 16.

schema.label: Eligible patient
schema.text: Post-menarchal female < 40 years, newly diagnosed first cancer (not breast carcinoma), with planned curative alkylating-agent chemotherapy. Cancer treatment itself is at the treating oncologist's discretion.

schema.text: Feasibility of a cross-network randomized trial of triptorelin in AYA females, and ovarian reserve by AMH 2 years after completion of alkylator-containing chemotherapy.

eligibility: Age < 40 years at enrollment; post-menarchal female with first menses > 6 months before enrollment.

Age < 20: expected cumulative cyclophosphamide equivalent dose ≥ 4 g/m2 (dacarbazine does not count). Age 20 to < 35: any dose of a CED-contributing alkylator. Age ≥ 35: any CED alkylator dose and/or dacarbazine.

Not pregnant, and not breastfeeding during triptorelin therapy (24 weeks per dose).

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG groupwide Phase 1/2 (US sites only) for relapsed, refractory, or progressive neuroblastoma after exactly one prior chemoimmunotherapy regimen. 28-day cycles, up to 12 cycles absent progression or unacceptable toxicity. Up to 76 patients.

schema.label: Backbone (DIN/CPM/Topo/GMCSF)
schema.text: Cyclophosphamide 250 mg/m2 IV and topotecan 0.75 mg/m2 IV days 1-5; dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2 IV over 10 hours days 2-5; sargramostim 250 mcg/m2 starting day 6 or 7 for at least 7 doses or until count recovery post-nadir.

schema.label: Phase 1 dose escalation
schema.text: Rolling six design adding enteral iberdomide to the backbone: dose level -1 0.4 mg/m2 (max 0.75 mg) days 1-14; level 1 0.6 mg/m2 (max 1 mg) days 1-14; level 2 0.6 mg/m2 (max 1 mg) days 1-21. Primary aim: RP2D.

schema.label: Phase 2 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified by MYCN status (amplified vs non-amplified/unknown) and relapsed vs refractory disease. Primary aim: response rate with vs without iberdomide.

arms.text: DIN/CPM/Topo/GMCSF.

eligibility: Age ≥ 1 and ≤ 30 years at enrollment.
Neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma by histology, or marrow tumor cells with urinary catecholamines > 2 x ULN, at initial diagnosis.

Primary refractory disease after at least 4 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy (as induction, extended induction, or pre-consolidation), or first relapse after induction or post-consolidation chemoimmunotherapy, or second relapse after chemoimmunotherapy given as first salvage.
Exactly one prior chemoimmunotherapy-containing regimen; a change in chemotherapy or anti-GD2 antibody counts as a second line.
No progression during or within 30 days of completing chemoimmunotherapy (last anti-GD2 dose) in induction or extended induction, and no stable disease after chemoimmunotherapy for first relapse.
Measurable MIBG-avid or FDG-avid soft tissue disease, or evaluable MIBG-avid lesions, or a new FDG-avid bone site with CT/MRI correlate or biopsy. No marrow-only or catecholamine-only disease.
Previously irradiated lesions count as targets only with progression after RT or viable tumor on post-RT biopsy.
Karnofsky or Lansky corresponding to ECOG 0-2.

Washouts: myelosuppressive chemotherapy 14 days; antibodies 21 days; small-port RT 7 days; large-field RT (TBI, CSI, whole abdomen, total lung, > 50% marrow) 12 weeks; other substantial marrow RT 6 weeks; autologous SCT 6 weeks.
No prior 131I-MIBG therapy for relapsed/refractory disease or poor end-of-induction response (frontline induction 131I-MIBG allowed after 6 weeks).
ANC ≥ 1000/µL and platelets ≥ 100,000/µL transfusion independent; creatinine within age limits or GFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 by direct measurement.
Bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, ALT ≤ 135 U/L; shortening fraction ≥ 27% or ejection fraction ≥ 50%.
No untreated CNS disease (adequately treated CNS disease without progression is allowed).
No prior allogeneic SCT, MDS, or other malignancy.
No pharmacologic systemic steroids within 7 days or expected need on study; no other immunosuppressants.
No permanent discontinuation of anti-GD2 therapy or GM-CSF for toxicity, no prior iberdomide, and no serious allergy to thalidomide, lenalidomide, or pomalidomide.
No enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants within 7 days or strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors within 14 days.
No prior unprovoked thrombosis; provoked events allowed if off anticoagulation or on a stable dose ≥ 6 weeks.
No peripheral neuropathy ≥ grade 2, no inability to take enteral medication, and not pregnant or breastfeeding; two contraception methods required with iberdomide.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: COG single-arm Phase 2 of tovorafenib (DAY101) in relapsed or refractory LCH with a RAS/RAF or receptor tyrosine kinase pathway mutation. Two cohorts: BRAFV600E positive (cohort 1, up to 26 evaluable) and BRAFV600E negative (cohort 2, up to 17 evaluable).

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Tovorafenib 380 mg/m2 (max 600 mg) enterally once weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22 of 28-day cycles, up to 12 cycles. Tablet or suspension (suspension required if BSA < 0.9 m2).

schema.label: Response evaluation
schema.text: Organ-specific imaging and FDG-PET at day 28 of cycles 2, 4, and 9 and at end of therapy.

schema.label: Primary aim
schema.text: Overall response rate after 2 cycles, maintained 4 weeks later, in each cohort. Secondary aims include toxicity, 1-year EFS, PFS, OS, and durability of CR after stopping therapy.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 28 days after end of therapy, then 3, 6, and 12 months and 2 years after cycle 12; off study at 5 years from enrollment.

eligibility: Age 180 days to < 22 years at enrollment; BSA ≥ 0.3 m2.

Histologically verified LCH (original diagnosis or relapse) that is progressive, relapsed, or refractory after at least one prior systemic treatment, with measurable disease. Pathology report due for central review within 7 days of enrollment.
Pathogenic somatic mutation in CSF1R, ERBB3, ALK, RAS, or RAF by PCR or sequencing (IHC alone not sufficient).
No activating MAP2K1 mutation.
No skin-limited disease, GI-only disease, or LCH-associated neurodegeneration without parenchymal or systemic lesions.
No LCH arising with another hematologic malignancy and no history of non-histiocytic malignancy.
Karnofsky or Lansky ≥ 50% (ECOG 0-2); able to take enteral medication.
Washouts: myelosuppressive chemotherapy 14 days; investigational or other anticancer therapy, including MAPK inhibitors, 14 days; RT 2 weeks from last fraction; prior toxicities ≤ grade 1.
Steroids ≤ 0.5 mg/kg/day prednisone equivalent (max 20 mg/day) averaged over the prior month; no strong CYP2C8 inducers or inhibitors or narrow-index BCRP substrates within 14 days.
ANC ≥ 750/µL, platelets ≥ 75,000/µL, hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL (transfusion allowed with documented marrow disease).
Creatinine within age limits or GFR ≥ 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, albumin ≥ 2 g/dL unless due to histiocytic liver disease.
Fractional shortening ≥ 25% or ejection fraction > 50%; no QTc > 440 ms, active cardiovascular disease, or MI, DVT, or PE within 6 months.
No known significant ophthalmologic condition or risk factors for retinal vein occlusion or central serous retinopathy.
No prior solid organ or hematopoietic transplant.
No grade ≥ 2 CNS hemorrhage history or any CNS hemorrhage within 28 days.
No major surgery within 14 days, uncontrolled infection, malabsorption, DRESS or SJS history, or grade 3 symptomatic CPK elevation.
Not pregnant or breastfeeding; non-hormonal contraception required for 28 days after the last dose.

schema.label: Enrollment
schema.text: Osteosarcoma with resectable oligometastatic lung disease (4 or fewer nodules per lung), newly diagnosed or at first pulmonary recurrence. Chest CT goes to rapid central imaging review within 5 days of enrollment to confirm eligibility and stratum.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Six groups: newly diagnosed poor risk vs average risk (poor risk: 2 or more metastases, bilateral lung metastases, or 10% or more viable tumor in the resected primary); recurrent poor risk vs average risk (poor risk: recurrence less than 18 months from diagnosis, 2 or more lesions, or bilateral), each split by whether post-thoracic-surgery chemotherapy is intended.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Surgical approach to pulmonary metastasectomy

arms.label: Open surgery
arms.text: Thoracotomy or sternotomy. Bilateral disease: sternotomy or bilateral thoracotomy, same day or staged with the second side within 8 weeks.

arms.label: Thoracoscopy
arms.text: Thoracoscopic (minimally invasive) resection of all pulmonary nodules.

schema.label: Systemic therapy
schema.text: Not protocol-directed. Newly diagnosed patients receive standard osteosarcoma chemotherapy (for example cisplatin-doxorubicin or ifosfamide-based) and standard primary local control; recurrent patients receive systemic therapy per the treating oncologist. Multitargeted TKIs must be held before surgery per label or institutional guidance.

schema.label: Post-operative assessment
schema.text: Chest CT 3 months after surgery (after the second operation if staged) to assess completeness of clearance; protocol therapy ends with this scan.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Thoracic event-free survival (intrathoracic recurrence on chest CT, or death from the procedure or a related complication). Secondary: EFS and OS. Target accrual reduced to a maximum of 62 patients with Amendment 3.

No prior therapeutic pulmonary surgery for lung metastasis.

schema.label: Feasibility phase (completed)
schema.text: Closed as of Amendment 2B. Metastatic osteosarcoma with resectable primary received cabozantinib plus MAP to define the combination dose; Dose Level 2 (35 mg/m2/day, max 60 mg, under 18; 60 mg daily for adults, concomitant with chemotherapy) carried into the efficacy phase.

schema.label: Efficacy phase (phase 2/3), cohort assignment
schema.text: Cohort 1 (standard risk): non-pelvic, non-metastatic, resectable primary. Cohort 2 (high risk): pelvic primary, unresectable primary, and/or metastatic disease. Randomization stratified by cohort.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1 within each cohort
schema.text: MAP vs cabozantinib plus MAP; all patients get dexrazoxane before doxorubicin and myeloid growth factor after cisplatin/doxorubicin cycles

arms.label: Regimen A (standard risk) / Regimen C (high risk): MAP
arms.text: Induction 2 cycles MAP (weeks 1-10), primary tumor surgery (weeks 11-12), Consolidation cycles 1-2 MAP and cycles 3-4 MA (methotrexate, doxorubicin), ending about week 33. High risk: metastasis resection after Consolidation cycle 1, additional local/metastatic management after Consolidation cycle 4.

arms.label: Regimen B (standard risk) / Regimen D (high risk): cabozantinib plus MAP
arms.text: Same MAP backbone with daily oral cabozantinib weeks 1-7 of Induction, held around surgery, resumed in Consolidation cycle 2 after wound healing (at least 2 weeks after thoracic surgery in high risk), then Maintenance cabozantinib alone for six 28-day cycles (weeks 34-58).

schema.label: Local control of residual or metastatic disease (high risk)
schema.text: After Consolidation cycle 4 and before Maintenance: surgery, SBRT, conventional or hypofractionated RT, or ablation to unresected metastatic sites; definitive or post-operative EBRT (photon or proton) for unresectable primary or positive margins.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Feasibility (completed); EFS for cabozantinib-MAP vs MAP, analyzed separately in standard-risk and high-risk cohorts. Phase 2: 374 patients (252 standard, 122 high risk), expanding to 996 for phase 3.

eligibility: Age under 40 years at enrollment; BSA greater than 0.8 m2.
Newly diagnosed high-grade osteosarcoma, any extremity or axial primary site; osteosarcoma as a second malignancy allowed if no prior systemic chemotherapy.

Efficacy phase: localized or metastatic disease regardless of resectability, assigned to standard-risk or high-risk cohort. Lung metastasis: biopsy-proven, or one or more lesions 5 mm or larger, or multiple lesions 3 mm or larger; suspicious bone lesions need biopsy or confirmatory MRI/CT.

Creatinine within age/sex limits (for example 1.7 mg/dL male and 1.4 mg/dL female at 16 years or older), or measured creatinine clearance or GFR 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher (eGFR not acceptable); bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less; ALT 135 U/L or less.
Shortening fraction 27% or higher or ejection fraction 50% or higher; QTcF under 480 msec; no congenital long QT, NYHA III-IV heart failure, unstable angina, or serious arrhythmia.
ANC 1000/uL or higher, platelets 100,000/uL or higher (transfusion independent), hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL or higher, INR 1.5 or less.
HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months and not on strong CYP3A4, CYP2D6, or MRP2 inhibitors/inducers.
No prior systemic therapy for osteosarcoma or a prior cancer.
No CNS metastases; no central cavitating pulmonary lesions invading or encasing major lung vessels.

No primary tumor resection or attempted curative metastasectomy before enrollment; no other major surgery within 14 days (diagnostic thoracoscopy and port placement allowed); no serious or non-healing wound or fracture (pathologic fracture of primary allowed).

No clinically significant GI bleeding, perforation, obstruction, abscess, or fistula within 6 months; no hemoptysis, pulmonary hemorrhage, or significant bleeding within 3 months; no bleeding diathesis.
No uncontrolled hypertension requiring medication (above 95th percentile for age under 18, above 140/90 mmHg at 18 or older), uncompensated hypothyroidism, or Child-Pugh B or C hepatic impairment.

No enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants within 14 days, strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors, QTc-prolonging drugs, or warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, or platelet inhibitors (low-dose aspirin and LMWH allowed; therapeutic LMWH, rivaroxaban, or apixaban allowed if stable for 6 weeks).
Must be able to swallow tablets whole; no malabsorption condition affecting cabozantinib.
Not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

schema.label: Enrollment
schema.text: Any child, adolescent, or young adult with a known or suspected eligible neoplasm, independent of therapeutic trial participation. Participants consent to one or more optional components. Some COG therapeutic trials require APEC14B1 enrollment first.

schema.label: Project:EveryChild components (COG sites)
schema.text: Six components: eligibility screening (clinical, pathology, imaging, surgical, and biologic data, with optional central review, for COG trial eligibility or risk stratification); biobanking of tumor, normal host, and parental germline specimens at diagnosis, progression, relapse, or post-mortem; tracking outcome; childhood cancer registry (formerly ACCRN07); contact for future research; and the Molecular Characterization Initiative.

schema.label: Project:AYA components (non-COG NCTN sites)
schema.text: Added in 2025 for adults potentially eligible for COG-led NCTN trials. Limited to eligibility screening, biobanking, future contact, and molecular characterization.

schema.label: Molecular Characterization Initiative
schema.text: NCI CCDI-sponsored testing for selected and rare cancer types at the Institute for Genomic Medicine: enhanced whole exome sequencing (tumor and germline), RNA fusion testing, and DNA methylation array. Results returned to the treating physician in about 3 weeks for clinical management and trial eligibility.

schema.label: Specimens
schema.text: Tumor only from clinically indicated procedures, never research-only procedures; research blood limited to 3 mL/kg or less (saliva or buccal swab in rare cases).

eligibility: Enrollment within 6 months of initial presentation, or within 6 months of refractory disease, progression, recurrence, second or secondary malignancy, or post-mortem.
Prior ACCRN07 patients may enroll in the tracking outcome, registry, and future contact components any time after reaching the age of majority.
Known or suspected neoplasm of the pediatric, adolescent, or young adult population: any ICD-O behavior code 1 (borderline), 2 (in situ), or 3 (malignant).
Any CNS or kidney neoplasm regardless of behavior.

Selected benign or borderline conditions: mesoblastic nephroma, teratomas (mature and immature), myeloproliferative disease including transient myeloproliferative disease, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, lymphoproliferative disease, desmoid tumors, gonadal stromal tumors, neuroendocrine tumors including pheochromocytoma, melanocytic tumors other than clearly benign nevi, and ganglioneuromas.
Age 25 years or younger at original diagnosis, except patients being screened for a specific COG (or COG-participating NCTN) therapeutic trial with a higher age limit.
Must agree to at least one study component; parents consent separately for their own specimens.

schema.label: Type II or III: progressive disease after window

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Enroll on APEC14B1 (Part A) and receive a qualifying Initial Stratum Assignment from central review (APEC14B1-REN) by Day 14 after nephrectomy or biopsy; enroll on AREN2231 by Day 14. Biology from a CLIA lab (LOH 1p and 16q, 1q gain; plus LOH 11p15 for potential mVLR) drives callbacks to the final regimen. Standard biology: no 1q gain and no combined LOH 1p/16q (Stage I: also no LOH 11p15; node-positive Stage III/IV: no single LOH 1p or 16q).

schema.label: Stage I
schema.text: Standard biology and either age under 4 (non-epithelial) or epithelial histology at any age: modified very low risk (mVLR), nephrectomy only. Adverse biology, or non-epithelial histology age 4 or older: EE-4A (vincristine, dactinomycin) cycles 1-7. mVLR relapse: DD-4A plus RT (flank/WAI, whole lung, or metastatic site) for FHWT, UH-3 for anaplasia.

schema.label: Stage II
schema.text: EE-4A cycle 1, then by biology: standard biology continues EE-4A cycles 2-7; adverse biology randomized.

schema.label: Randomize (Stage II adverse biology)
schema.text: Cycles 2-9

arms.label: DD-4A
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin.

arms.label: VIVA
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, irinotecan (EE-4A backbone plus vincristine/irinotecan cycles).

schema.label: Stage III
schema.text: Upfront nephrectomy: DD-4A cycle 1 with abdominal RT; standard biology moves to EE-4A from cycle 2 (doxorubicin omitted), adverse biology randomized M vs MVI. Biopsy/delayed nephrectomy: DD-4A cycles 1-2, delayed nephrectomy after cycle 2 (or after cycle 3-4), then by histology and biology: standard biology with low/intermediate-risk histology continues EE-4A or DD-4A, adverse biology randomized M vs MVI, high-risk blastemal-predominant histology goes to UH-3. Most Stage III patients receive RT.

schema.label: Stage IV
schema.text: DD-4A cycles 1-2, then central lung response assessment. Lung-only, standard biology, rapid complete response (RCR): continue DD-4A without lung RT. Lung-only with slow incomplete response (SIR) or adverse biology, and all extrapulmonary metastases: randomized M vs MVI with whole lung and/or metastatic site RT. High-risk histology at delayed nephrectomy: UH-3. Most Stage IV patients receive RT.

schema.label: Randomize (Stage III adverse biology; Stage IV SIR, adverse biology, or extrapulmonary metastases)

arms.label: Regimen M
arms.text: Vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, etoposide (starts at Cycle 3).

arms.label: Regimen MVI
arms.text: Regimen M plus vincristine/irinotecan cycles (starts at Cycle 3).

schema.label: Radiation therapy
schema.text: Flank RT 10.8 Gy/6 fx (19.8 Gy/11 fx for high-risk histology at delayed nephrectomy); whole abdomen 10.5 Gy/7 fx for rupture, diffuse spill, or peritoneal seeding; whole lung 12 Gy/8 fx (10.5 Gy/7 fx age 12 months or younger); brain, liver, bone, node, and soft tissue metastasis doses per section 17.9.4. Abdominal RT begins by Day 14 after nephrectomy; lung RT after the cycle 2 response assessment. IROC pre-approval required for whole lung IMRT, liver RT, and proton flank or WAI.

schema.label: Primary aims
schema.text: EFS: maintain outcomes with treatment reduction (Stage I nephrectomy only, Stage III EE-4A non-inferiority); non-inferiority of VIVA vs DD-4A (Stage II adverse biology) and MVI vs M (Stage III/IV); superiority of UH-3 for blastemal-predominant Stage III/IV vs historical controls.

No prior tumor-directed chemotherapy or radiotherapy for this diagnosis (except emergent therapy); no prior doxorubicin if doxorubicin may be required; no concurrent chemotherapy for another diagnosis.

Not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

eligibility: Male, age ≥ 18 years.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma, or no histology but PSA > 100 ng/mL with radiographic metastatic disease at diagnosis.
Metastatic disease on conventional imaging (bone scan, CT, or MRI) or PSMA-PET at ADT initiation. PSA ≥ 2.0 ng/mL before starting ADT (for histologically confirmed cases).
ADT for mCSPC for at least 6 and no more than 12 months (± 3 weeks) at enrollment, and an ARPI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, or darolutamide) for at least 4 months (± 2 weeks).
Prior radiotherapy to the prostate bed and/or metastatic sites allowed, with recovery to grade ≤ 1. Persistent stable ADT toxicities (hot flushes, fatigue) of any grade allowed.
Serum testosterone < 1.7 nmol/L (50 ng/dL) and PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL within 28 days of enrollment.
Candidate for docetaxel. ECOG performance status 0-2.

Within 28 days: hemoglobin ≥ 80 g/L, ANC ≥ 1.5 x 10^9/L, platelets ≥ 100 x 10^9/L, total bilirubin ≤ 1.0 x ULN (≤ 2.0 x ULN if Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤ 1.5 x ULN with alkaline phosphatase ≤ 2.5 x ULN, creatinine clearance ≥ 30 mL/min.
No confirmed PSA progression on ADT (25% rise above nadir and an absolute rise of 2.0 ng/mL, confirmed by a further 25% rise at least 3 weeks later).
No confirmed radiographic or clinical progression since starting ADT (new bone lesions judged to be flare are allowed).
No prior taxane chemotherapy, no grade ≥ 2 peripheral neuropathy, and no severe hypersensitivity to polysorbate 80 formulations.
No unstable angina, symptomatic pericarditis, or MI within 6 months, and no NYHA class III-IV heart failure.
No concurrent anticancer systemic therapy other than ADT and ARPI. No live vaccine within 30 days.
No high-grade neuroendocrine or small cell features (except patients enrolled without histology on the PSA > 100 ng/mL criterion).
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV must have undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must be treated and cured, or viral load undetectable if on treatment.

No prior chemotherapy for this cancer, no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, no contraindication to chemotherapy or ribociclib.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load and CD4 > 250 cells/mcL; chronic HBV allowed if viral load undetectable on suppressive therapy; HCV allowed if treated with undetectable viral load.

eligibility: Pathologically or cytologically proven NSCLC; mixed NSCLC histologies allowed, but no known small cell component.

Pre-screening: tissue available for on-study profiling; currently on, or previously received, first-line standard therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease and not yet progressed on the current or most recent line. Patients using prior biomarker results cannot be pre-screened. Patients on osimertinib aiming for S1900G must not be pre-screened.

Screening at progression: at least one prior line of standard systemic therapy for stage I-IV NSCLC with progression during or after the most recent line. If no prior therapy for stage IV or recurrent disease, progression must have occurred ≤ 180 days after the last dose of stage I-III systemic therapy; if > 180 days, standard therapy for advanced disease and progression on it are required first.

Screening at progression biomarker route: tissue for on-study profiling, an approved prior NGS report, or a non-listed NGS report (or specific biomarker documentation) accepted by e-mail from LUNGMAPNGS@swog.org. For EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified disease screening for S1900G, tissue must be obtained after progression on osimertinib.

Treatment-naive route: no prior systemic therapy for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC and documentation (approved or e-mail-accepted NGS report) of a biomarker for a sub-study open to treatment-naive patients. Do not submit tissue for this route.

Tissue for on-study testing: FFPE block, or 12 unstained slides plus an H&E (or 13 unstained slides) at 4-5 microns, with ≥ 20% tumor cells and ≥ 0.2 mm3 tumor volume; no decalcified bone biopsies (cell blocks of pleural fluid acceptable). Consent to Foundation Medicine testing and banking of leftover tissue.

Prior test reports: full report available, tissue or blood specified, original report dated on or after September 1, 2019, from a CLIA/CAP/ISO-certified lab (non-listed tests need gene list and e-mail approval). A blood-only NGS report must show at least one alteration on the Genomic Alterations Form, otherwise tissue testing is required.

eligibility: Female, age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2 (or Karnofsky 60% or more).

Premenopausal: age 50 or under with menses within 12 months; age >50-60 with menses within 12 months plus premenopausal FSH and estradiol; or premenopausal FSH and estradiol if amenorrheic from IUD, uterine ablation, or prior hysterectomy.
Resected pT1-3 (T1c or higher if N0), pN0 or pN1 (pN1mi, pN1a-c) by AJCC 8th edition. ITCs count as N0; micrometastases (0.2-2 mm) count as N1.

Oncotype DX RS: pN0 requires RS 21-25, or RS 16-20 with high clinical risk; pN1 (1-3 nodes) requires RS below 26. MammaPrint Low Risk/MP1 patients need central Oncotype testing; MammaPrint High Risk/MP2 ineligible.
ER and/or PgR positive (1% or more by IHC) and HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP, local testing.

Lumpectomy, or total, skin-sparing, or nipple-sparing mastectomy. Lumpectomy margins free of invasive cancer and DCIS (no ink on tumor; positive posterior margin allowed if no further resection possible; LCIS at margin allowed). Mastectomy margins free of gross tumor; microscopic positive margin allowed if chest wall PMRT is planned.
Axillary staging by sentinel node biopsy, targeted axillary dissection, or ALND.
No more than 16 weeks from last breast surgery (including re-excision) to pre-entry.
Synchronous ipsilateral or contralateral, multifocal, or multicentric cancer allowed if the highest-stage tumor qualifies and other sites would not need chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy.

No prior RT, chemotherapy, or biotherapy for the current breast cancer. Endocrine therapy for this cancer limited to less than 6 weeks (neoadjuvant or adjuvant). Prior preventive tamoxifen and AI or GnRH for fertility preservation allowed.
No metastatic disease, pT4 or inflammatory breast cancer, or non-epithelial breast malignancy (sarcoma, lymphoma).
No prior invasive breast cancer in either breast (prior DCIS or LCIS allowed; prior ipsilateral DCIS treated with lumpectomy and RT requires mastectomy for the current cancer).
No life expectancy under 10 years from comorbidity.

No ANC below 1,200/mm3, platelets below 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, bilirubin above ULN (above 1.5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT above 3 x ULN, or GFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 on most recent routine labs.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be treated and cured or have undetectable viral load on therapy.
Prior or concurrent non-breast malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Hormonal contraception (including progestin IUDs) must be stopped before pre-entry. Not pregnant and not nursing.

At least one intact ovary and fallopian tube at counseling, consent, and registration. Prior hysterectomy allowed if it did not include bilateral salpingectomy; prior tubal ligation allowed if one ovary and tube with fimbria remain.
Pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal preferred) or pelvic MRI and CA-125 within 180 days before registration.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Early-stage oral cavity SCC, cT1-2N0 (AJCC 8th ed.). FDG PET/CT with central read.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration
schema.text: PET/CT node negative patients proceed to randomization. PET/CT node positive patients go off study (neck pathology recorded in a registry).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Clinical and radiographic T stage (T1 vs T2); Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1-2).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Primary tumor resection (transoral, aiming for 5 mm margins) and neck surgery in the same operation, within 30 days after central PET/CT review.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy with planar and mandatory SPECT/CT lymphatic mapping. Positive SLN leads to completion neck dissection (at least levels I-III) within 6 weeks, ideally 4.

arms.label: Arm 2 (control)
arms.text: Elective neck dissection, at least levels I-III (bilateral for lesions within 1 cm of midline).

schema.label: Adjuvant therapy (both arms, by final pathology)
schema.text: Observation if no adverse features. Adjuvant IMRT alone for PNI, LVI, pT3/T4, close margins (< 5 mm), or pN1+ (sites may omit RT for pN1 as the only risk factor). Adjuvant chemoradiation with concurrent cisplatin (every 3 weeks or weekly) for positive margins or extranodal extension. RT covers both primary site and at-risk neck: 60 Gy in 30 fractions (PTV_6000), 56 Gy in 30 (PTV_5600), 66 Gy in 30 (PTV_6600) when used. IMRT and IGRT mandatory, protons not allowed; adjuvant treatment starts within 42 days after surgery.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Phase II: patient-reported neck and shoulder function (NDII) at 6 months after surgery. Phase III: non-inferiority of disease-free survival plus NDII at 6 months.

schema.label: Sample size
schema.text: Phase II 258; phase III 686 total including phase II patients.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: EBV-associated recurrent and/or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, no prior palliative systemic therapy.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration and induction
schema.text: Baseline plasma EBV DNA collected. Induction within 7 days: nivolumab 360 mg IV Day 1 + cisplatin 80 mg/m2 (or carboplatin AUC 5) Day 1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8, every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Response by RECIST 1.1 after cycles 3 and 6.

schema.label: Step 3: Registration
schema.text: Patients without progression (CR, PR, SD) after 3-6 induction cycles completed within 20 weeks, with post-induction plasma EBV DNA collected. Patients with progression go off study.

arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks.

arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg + relatlimab (BMS-986016) 480 mg as a single IV infusion every 4 weeks.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically proven NPC with locoregional recurrence not amenable to curative surgery or re-irradiation, and/or distant metastases (de novo metastatic allowed).
EBV associated: EBER-positive tumor, or a history of detectable plasma EBV DNA by PCR at any time since diagnosis.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 (previously irradiated lesions count only with documented progression after RT); contrast CT chest, and contrast CT or MRI of nasopharynx and neck if locoregional disease is known.

Treated brain or leptomeningeal metastases or cord compression allowed if clinically stable ≥ 2 months and off steroids (> 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent) > 4 weeks; skull base involvement allowed unless directly invading brain with symptoms or significant edema.
Age ≥ 18; ECOG 0-2.
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 8.0 g/dL (transfusion allowed, not EPO dependent).
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN or direct bilirubin ≤ ULN (≤ 3 x ULN with Gilbert's); ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases); corrected calcium ≤ 1.5 x ULN.
Creatinine ≤ 1.5 x ULN or CrCl > 30 mL/min; CrCl must be > 50 mL/min for cisplatin (carboplatin if 30-50).

No prior palliative systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic NPC (prior curative-intent therapy, including systemic therapy before curative re-irradiation or surgery, allowed); > 6 months from last curative-intent treatment to recurrence.
No prior PD-L1, PD-L2, LAG-3, or other checkpoint/co-stimulation agents; prior PD-1 or CTLA-4 inhibitor allowed only as adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy for non-metastatic NPC.
Prior therapy toxicity resolved to grade 0-1 (except alopecia, dry mouth, dysgeusia, dysphagia, fatigue; cisplatin neuropathy must be grade 0-2; any hearing loss allowed).
No palliative RT within 30 days unless the irradiated sites are not target lesions and not the only measurable disease; no major surgery within 30 days.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization or MI within 6 months; NYHA II or better; no prior myocarditis.
No history of pneumonitis requiring steroids, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or organizing pneumonia; no active or MDR TB (treated TB > 2 years ago allowed); no active infection requiring IV therapy.

No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 2 years (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hormone-replaced endocrinopathy, alopecia, and psoriasis not requiring systemic therapy allowed); no immunosuppressive steroids (> 10 mg prednisone) or immunosuppressants within 14 days; no prior solid organ or bone marrow transplant.
No live vaccine within 30 days; no grade 3-4 allergy to cisplatin, carboplatin, or gemcitabine, or grade 4 reaction to any monoclonal antibody.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months at an experienced site; chronic HBV requires undetectable HBV DNA; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

Step 3: no progression after a minimum of 3 and up to 6 induction cycles completed within 20 weeks of Cycle 1 Day 1 (fewer than 6 only for toxicity delays or intercurrent illness), CT within 30 days, no criteria for permanent discontinuation or nivolumab-related autoimmune toxicity requiring discontinuation, and post-induction plasma EBV DNA collected.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration
schema.text: Central LVEF ≥ 50% confirmed; register within 21 days of ECHO submission. Cohort assigned by current beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor use.

schema.text: Patients not on these agents were randomized (stratified by prior anthracycline and central LVEF 50-54% vs ≥ 55%) to Arm 1, carvedilol 6.25 mg PO twice daily for 108 weeks, or Arm 2, no prophylaxis. Arms 1 and 2 are permanently closed to accrual as of Revision 7.

schema.label: Endpoint assessment
schema.text: Cardiac dysfunction by central ECHO Core Lab read and predefined cardiac events; HER2 therapy continuation is at physician discretion.

schema.label: Primary objective
schema.text: 2-year cumulative incidence of cardiac dysfunction and/or predefined cardiac events in patients on trastuzumab-based therapy plus a beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor, and a risk prediction model from clinical factors and biomarkers.

eligibility: Metastatic breast cancer, starting within 11 days of Step 1 or continuing trastuzumab-based HER2-targeted therapy in the first- to fourth-line metastatic setting (trastuzumab or biosimilar with or without chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, pertuzumab, lapatinib, or tucatinib; T-DM1; trastuzumab deruxtecan). No limit on prior HER2 doses.
No lapatinib without trastuzumab, and no planned concurrent anthracycline with HER2 therapy.
Brain metastases allowed.

Increased cardiotoxicity risk: prior anthracycline, or at least one of LVEF 50-54% on local ECHO, age ≥ 65, BMI ≥ 30, current or prior antihypertensive therapy, coronary artery disease, diabetes, or atrial fibrillation/flutter.
Observation cohort (Arm 3, the only open arm): currently taking a beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor at Step 1. (Closed randomized arms required no such agent within 21 days.)
LVEF ≥ 50% by 2D or 3D ECHO within 28 days, done at the site's validated ECHO lab and confirmed by central read before Step 2; follow-up ECHOs must include 2D images.
Age ≥ 18; Zubrod performance status 0-2; history and physical within 28 days.
Bilirubin < 3.0 x ULN, AST/ALT < 5.0 x ULN within 28 days; not dialysis dependent.

No other prior malignancy except treated basal or squamous skin cancer, cervical carcinoma in situ, prostate cancer on active surveillance, treated stage I-II cancer in complete remission, or any cancer disease free for 5 years.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Willing to submit blood specimens.

schema.label: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Previously treated stage IV or recurrent NSCLC screened on the Lung-MAP master protocol; not eligible for a biomarker-matched sub-study and assigned to S1800E as a non-match sub-study.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Histology (squamous or mixed vs non-squamous); Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 21-day cycles starting within 7 days of randomization, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or treatment delay > 84 days. Randomization ratio not stated in the protocol text.

arms.label: Arm A (control)
arms.text: Ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV Day 1 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV Day 1 (60 mg/m2 allowed) every 21 days, with dexamethasone premedication.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Ramucirumab + docetaxel as in Arm A + cemiplimab 350 mg IV Day 1 every 21 days. Cycle 1 safety run-in with weekly toxicity checks.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival (phase III), with a phase II interim futility analysis on PFS at 99 events. Accrual goal 378.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after randomization.

eligibility: Registered to LUNGMAP, not eligible for a biomarker-matched sub-study, and assigned to S1800E by the SDMC.
Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before randomization (non-measurable disease assessed within 42 days). Disease limited to a prior RT port must show clear progression.
Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before randomization.

Exactly one prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 regimen for advanced disease; perioperative PD-1/PD-L1 counts if progression occurred ≤ 365 days from its start. Progression > 84 days after starting the most recent PD-1/PD-L1 regimen, with best response of SD, PR, or CR if given for stage IV disease.
Prior platinum-based chemotherapy with progression; at least one prior targeted therapy if an actionable alteration is present.
No prior docetaxel.
No palliative RT within 14 days before randomization (bone RT within 7 days).
No major surgery within 28 days or port placement within 7 days; no wound-healing complications within 2 months; no nonhealing wound or fracture within 28 days.

ANC ≥ 1,500/mcL, hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL, platelets ≥ 100,000/mcL; total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases); CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min; urine protein within 28 days.
Zubrod performance status 0-1 by H&P within 28 days before randomization.
HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; HBV and HCV allowed with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No prior or concurrent malignancy likely to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 60 days; no primary immunodeficiency.
No prior grade ≥ 3 immune-related AE (except asymptomatic rash), unresolved grade 2 irAE, or toxicity leading to permanent PD-1/PD-L1 discontinuation (endocrinopathy on stable replacement allowed).
No transplant requiring immunosuppression, live vaccine within 28 days, active TB, or pneumonitis or ILD that required steroids.

No GI perforation or fistula within 6 months, GI bleeding within 3 months, or arterial thromboembolism within 6 months; no NYHA class III/IV heart failure, unstable angina or MI within 6 months, or uncontrolled arrhythmia.
No gross hemoptysis (≥ 1/2 teaspoon) within 2 months, tumor cavitation, or major blood vessel invasion.
No VTE within 3 months; VTE more than 3 months earlier must be on stable anticoagulation.
No Child-Pugh B or worse cirrhosis with hepatic encephalopathy or clinically meaningful ascites, or any degree of cirrhosis (as written).
Not pregnant or breastfeeding. Agrees to ctDNA blood submission.

schema.text: Screened on the LUNGMAP master protocol at radiographic or clinical progression on osimertinib; tissue for biomarker profiling, or tissue or blood (ctDNA) NGS results from an accepted CLIA laboratory, obtained after progression on osimertinib. SWOG SDMC assigns eligible EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified participants to S1900G.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Brain metastases (yes vs no); prior lines of therapy for advanced, recurrent, or metastatic disease (1 vs 2 or more).

schema.label: Step 2: S1900G randomization 1:1
schema.text: Treatment starts within 10 calendar days of sub-study randomization. 28-day cycles until progression or other removal criteria. Safety run-in: first 10 eligible treated participants per arm, with weekly adverse event evaluation in Cycle 1.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Capmatinib 400 mg PO twice daily, days 1-28, plus osimertinib 80 mg PO daily, days 1-28, plus ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Capmatinib 400 mg PO twice daily, days 1-28, plus osimertinib 80 mg PO daily, days 1-28.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after sub-study randomization, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Key secondary: Cycle 1 toxicity rate, grade 2 or higher edema, weight change from baseline.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900G by the SWOG SDMC through the LUNGMAP screening protocol.
NSCLC with a sensitizing EGFR mutation, with radiologic or clinical progression on osimertinib (alone or in combination) as the most recent line of therapy; any number of prior lines allowed.
MET amplification by tissue- or blood-based (ctDNA) NGS in a CLIA, ISO/IEC, CAP, or similarly certified laboratory, on tissue or blood obtained after progression on osimertinib.

Measurable disease (assessed within 28 days) or non-measurable disease (within 42 days) by CT or MRI before sub-study randomization. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts as measurable only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT with contrast or MRI within 42 days before sub-study randomization. Symptomatic CNS metastases (brain or leptomeningeal) allowed if neurologically stable with stable or decreasing steroids for at least 5 days.
Able to tolerate osimertinib 80 mg daily for at least 14 days before sub-study randomization (rechallenge at 80 mg may be considered after a prior dose reduction).
No prior MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor (prior anti-MET antibody such as amivantamab allowed).

No anti-cancer drug other than osimertinib within 21 days (osimertinib may continue to the day before study treatment); no radiation therapy within 14 days; no major surgery within 14 days; no live attenuated vaccine within 28 days before sub-study randomization. No planned concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity (except alopecia and vitiligo).
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before sub-study randomization. Able to swallow tablets whole.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin above 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 2.5 x ULN (AST up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).

ECG with QTcF of 470 msec or less within 28 days. Urine protein 1+ or less on dipstick or UA (if 2+ or more, 24-hour urine protein below 1000 mg). INR no more than 1.5 seconds and PTT no more than 5 seconds above the institutional ULN unless anticoagulated.
Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better.

No signs or symptoms of pancreatitis or pancreatic injury (asymptomatic amylase or lipase elevation allowed). No uncontrolled blood pressure or hypertension within 28 days, as judged by the treating investigator.
No moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers (including St. John's Wort) within 7 days before sub-study registration or during treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission.

schema.text: Screened on the LUNGMAP master protocol; tissue for biomarker profiling, or tissue or blood (ctDNA) results from a CLIA, ISO/IEC, CAP, or similarly certified laboratory. SWOG SDMC assigns MET amplification-positive participants to S1900J.

schema.text: Treatment starts within 10 calendar days of sub-study registration. Participants with non-FoundationOne test results submit archival tissue for retrospective FoundationOne testing.

schema.text: Amivantamab 1,600 mg/hyaluronidase 20,000 units if under 80 kg, or 2,240 mg/28,000 units if 80 kg or more (baseline weight). Weekly in Cycle 1 (days 1, 8, 15, 22), then days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle until progression or other removal criteria.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after sub-study registration, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Objective response rate (confirmed and unconfirmed, complete and partial) within each cohort.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900J by the SWOG SDMC based on NSCLC with MET amplification in LUNGMAP, identified by on-study tumor testing or documented from a prior tissue- or blood-based NGS test on the approved list.
No other known actionable oncogenic alteration (EGFR sensitizing or T790M, MET exon 14 skipping, ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK, HER2 mutation, KRAS G12C, BRAF V600E, among others).

Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before sub-study registration (non-measurable sites within 42 days). Effusions, ascites, or labs alone do not qualify. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts as measurable only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before sub-study registration. Asymptomatic CNS metastases (brain or leptomeningeal) allowed if clinically stable and asymptomatic for at least 14 days; prednisone 10 mg or less (or equivalent) for at least 14 days is allowed.
At least one prior line of systemic therapy for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC, with progression on the most recent line.
No prior MET TKI (tepotinib, capmatinib, crizotinib, etc.) for any cancer.

No systemic therapy (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, investigational drug) within 21 days; no anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody within 6 weeks; no radiation therapy within 14 days before sub-study registration. No planned concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.
No major surgery (other than vascular access or biopsy) or significant trauma within 28 days, and no surgery planned during the study.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity, except known permanent effects (for example immunotherapy endocrinopathy, cisplatin neurotoxicity).
Zubrod performance status 0-2 within 28 days before sub-study registration.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin at least 10.0 g/dL, platelets at least 75 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); serum creatinine at or below ULN or creatinine clearance at least 45 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No history of pneumonitis requiring drug therapy and no active symptomatic ILD/pneumonitis, including drug-induced or radiation pneumonitis.

Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy within 6 months; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load within 6 months if on treatment. No other clinically active infectious liver disease.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better. No clinically significant hypertension within 28 days. Known diabetes must be controlled within 14 days.

No active bleeding diathesis, no continuous oxygen requirement, and no unstable ophthalmologic condition. Infections needing antimicrobials must finish treatment within 7 days before starting study treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing; negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days if of reproductive potential.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission, and archival tissue (if available) when MET amplification came from a non-Foundation Medicine test.

schema.label: Step 2: S1900N randomization (3 arms)
schema.text: 35 eligible participants per arm (105 eligible, 117 enrolled). Treatment starts within 10 calendar days of randomization. 21-day cycles until progression or other removal criteria (any radiation therapy removes the participant from protocol treatment). Arm 1 has a safety run-in with weekly toxicity checks in Cycle 1.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV day 1, then (after at least 30 minutes of observation) sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8, every 21 days.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8, every 21 days.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV day 1, every 21 days.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after randomization, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS for Arm 1 vs Arm 2 and Arm 1 vs Arm 3; response rate (confirmed and unconfirmed, complete and partial) of each arm against historical single-agent chemotherapy.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900N by the SWOG SDMC based on stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with an actionable genomic alteration: an activating driver with an approved lung cancer targeted therapy in ALK, EGFR, HER2 (ERBB2), MET, NTRK, RET, or ROS1.
Prior appropriate targeted therapy for the alteration and prior platinum-based chemotherapy for stage IV or recurrent disease, with progression during or after the most recent systemic therapy.
No more than 3 prior lines of cytotoxic therapy (chemotherapy or antibody-drug conjugates) for NSCLC.
No prior TROP2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate or sacituzumab govitecan/SN-38-containing therapy, and no prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody.

No systemic lung cancer therapy within 21 days before randomization (oral agents within 10 days). Prior radiation therapy must be completed before randomization (7-day rule; see notes). No planned concurrent systemic lung cancer therapy.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity (except alopecia).

Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before randomization (non-measurable sites within 42 days). Effusions, ascites, or labs alone do not qualify. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before randomization. Brain metastases or cord compression allowed without residual neurologic dysfunction (unless no further recovery is expected and on weaning steroids, prednisone 10 mg daily or less); lesions needing local treatment must be treated and controlled and asymptomatic for at least 7 days after stereotactic radiation or 14 days after whole brain radiation.
No leptomeningeal disease requiring CNS-specific treatment before randomization or planned during the study.
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before randomization.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin at least 10.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No arterial or venous thrombotic event or hemoptysis within 28 days before randomization. No planned warfarin or other coumadin derivatives during treatment.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better.

Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy within 6 months; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load within 6 months if on treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission.
